answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on the backs, remove cards targeting colors not in play, and keep each player's own Ambush. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: IDs upright in stands; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, values hidden.

answers.answer: There is no individual player-by-player turn order. Players may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is needed. The player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, so Red is the sole Target with three votes versus two each for Blue and Green.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player survives the voting requirement if they voted for either tied Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: all players tied for most votes are Targets; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: every non-Target who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception. Green voted for Red rather than the sole Target, Blue, and did not Ambush.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to successful Ambush.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one, so Red and Yellow tie for most votes and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red may eliminate a player who voted for Red, namely Yellow. Pink voted for a tied Target (Yellow), so Pink survives. Red and Pink survive.
answers.evidence: The three-player illustration states Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes Red, and Pink votes Yellow; Red and Yellow tie as Targets, Red can retaliate only against Yellow, and Pink survives, leaving Red and Pink.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets its player choose one player who voted for them to eliminate; it does not eliminate all four voters. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: a successful ambusher “chooses one of the players who voted for them” and cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the survivors; only surviving players participate in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: three or more survivors “continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. Components: Gold Bars are cards, with values of 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; after any discussion or bargain, each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal their choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go, chooses one face down, and both reveal simultaneously when ready.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar, even if eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with no survivors, each player not participating in the final vote gets one deck bar; leave the four central bars for next round and add no new bars. Special Rules clarifies final voters get no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player receives zero cards and the Steal player receives all four central cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: Share player gets 0; opponent gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one card and the Steal player receives the other three central cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Steal gives the chooser 1 and the opponent 3; the rule says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one card and the Share player receives the other three central cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Share gives the chooser 1 and the opponent 3; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two remain in the center, and if play continues add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, each gets one and the other two remain; add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: double Steal means neither finalist gets gold; every other player gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded. The threshold is at least 25 points with 6–9 players and at least 24 points with 10–12 players. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: check “at the end of a round,” after awards; 25 points for 6–9 players, 24 for 10–12; if multiple qualify, the highest total wins.

answers.answer: The booklet's instruction, as summarized, is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. It does not provide a procedure or card arrangement for three or more tied leaders. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns for the next round, including players eliminated earlier; all Player IDs are stood upright again.
answers.evidence: Scoring says tied totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total; the source limitation says no arrangement is supplied for three or more. Turn Structure says everyone returns if there is no winner.

answers.answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; any method is allowed, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, and texting; the game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: Choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself because you suspect you are the Target, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; target with the card matching that player's visible ID color; play your Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: If no one wins, keep any central bars left over and refill the pool to four by dealing only enough new bars to reach four, face down with values hidden. If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.
answers.evidence: After round rewards, refill to four as needed; bars left behind remain. Deal new bars face down; deal four if the pot was entirely awarded, otherwise add only enough to bring the pool to four.

answers.answer: No. Blue remains the sole Target with four votes versus Purple's three; Blue's successful Ambush lets Blue survive but does not change who the Target is. Voters for Purple did not vote for the Target, so they do not survive on that basis (absent a successful Ambush exception).
answers.evidence: Vote: the player receiving the most votes is the Target; Ambush cards do not count as votes. Ambush: success protects its Target, and it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.” Vote: non-Targets who did not vote for any Target are eliminated, subject to successful Ambush.

answers.answer: The instruction is to have tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. The summary says the booklet does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two tied players; that procedure is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary; source limitation: no arrangement for three or more players tied for highest qualifying total is supplied.

answers.answer: Yes, conditionally: if the outsider receives the compensation bar and thereby has the single highest total, the winner is the player with the highest point total, and the tie instruction seeks one player anywhere at the table with the highest total. The summary says double Steal awards every player other than the finalists one deck bar. It also notes the booklet does not specify how to supply the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns, so whether that compensation applies in that extra showdown context is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Double Steal: every other player gets one bar from the deck. Scoring: the highest point total wins and extra Showdowns repeat until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Source limitation: the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns is unspecified.
